items.finding: The authorization flow omits the nonce parameter required by OpenID Connect to prevent replay attacks.
Accounts are linked by matching email addresses without verifying the email_verified claim, enabling account takeover if an IdP provides unverified emails.
Session tokens stored in browser localStorage violate the security policy that prohibits localStorage for tokens and requires HTTP-only cookies.
90-day session duration exceeds the 30-day maximum specified in the security policy, increasing exposure window from account takeover incidents.
Sessions persist without back-channel revocation checks despite the security policy requiring them when supported, allowing continued access after IdP revocation.
JWKS fetched once at deploy and cached indefinitely contradicts the configuration template requiring refresh every 24 hours minimum, risking signature validation failures after key rotation.
Wildcard redirect URI pattern allows any subdomain to receive authentication codes, enabling potential open redirect attacks if subdomains are compromised.

State parameter described as 32 bytes but RFC 6749 recommends a minimum of 128 bits (16 bytes) with 256 bits (32 bytes) being reasonable for high-security applications, though not strictly a violation.
